extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (novelists and short-story writers), users of Novlr looking to improve their story endings
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and concrete steps for crafting and evaluating satisfying endings to short stories and novels, including essential elements, types of endings, planning and discovery strategies, and a testing checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising yet inevitable
rubrics_metrics.description: An ending should feel both surprising and inevitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best endings 'catch readers off guard while making complete sense within the context of your story.' Aim for an ending that readers did not see coming but that, in retrospect, feels like the only plausible conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve the main conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Give readers the closure they’ve been anticipating throughout your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ending should address and resolve the story's central conflict so readers feel the narrative arc has reached a conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete character arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how your characters have grown or changed through their journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate meaningful change or development in key characters by the story's conclusion so the emotional and psychological journey feels finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver on story promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay off the expectations you’ve built through the rest of the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the narrative promises, clues and foreshadowing you established earlier and ensure the ending responds to reader expectations rather than ignoring them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect core themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinforce the deeper meanings, themes, and messages of your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ending should echo and illuminate the story's main themes, giving the reader a sense of the work's underlying ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide emotional payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Make readers feel their investment in your story was worthwhile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver an ending that rewards readers emotionally — whether with catharsis, melancholy, joy, or ambiguity — so they feel satisfied by the experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feel earned, not forced
rubrics_metrics.description: Arise naturally from the events and choices that came before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid contrived resolutions or deus ex machina; an earned ending grows logically from characters' decisions and plot developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match ending type to story needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose an ending style that grows naturally from your story’s genre, themes, and character journeys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lighthearted romance may call for a neat resolution; a philosophical literary novel might suit ambiguity. Consider genre expectations and thematic fit when selecting an ending style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution endings
rubrics_metrics.description: Endings that tie up all major plot threads neatly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works well for standalone novels, genre fiction where readers expect closure, stories with clear antagonists, and traditional narrative structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open endings
rubrics_metrics.description: Endings where some questions remain unanswered, inviting reader interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for literary fiction, stories focusing on internal conflict, works emphasising life's complexity, or those aiming for realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular endings
rubrics_metrics.description: The story returns to where it began but with meaningful change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective in character-driven narratives, coming-of-age stories, and tales about cycles or personal growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twist endings
rubrics_metrics.description: An unexpected revelation changes everything that came before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works well in mystery and crime novels, psychological thrillers, stories with unreliable narrators, or narratives exploring perception vs reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bittersweet endings
rubrics_metrics.description: Victory comes at a cost, combining triumph with loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate for epic narratives, war stories, complex moral tales, and stories about sacrifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epilogue endings
rubrics_metrics.description: A glimpse into the future after the main conflict resolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for series conclusions, generational stories, or works needing extra emotional closure or to show far-reaching consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot your ending first (for planners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a clear destination to help you plant the right seeds throughout your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning the ending ahead makes foreshadowing and structural setup easier and allows you to craft an ending that feels inevitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an ending outline (for planners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map out the major beats of your conclusion chapter by chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An outline helps ensure pacing and that each necessary beat toward resolution is covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant deliberate clues / foreshadowing
rubrics_metrics.description: Weave in foreshadowing that will make your ending feel inevitable in retrospect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hints and setup throughout the story so the ending's revelations or resolutions feel earned rather than sudden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track your promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a list of questions your story raises that readers will want answered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a running checklist of plot points and narrative promises to ensure you address them by the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write multiple endings (for discovery writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore different possible conclusions without committing to one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting several endings can reveal which feels truest to the characters and themes; it's a low-risk way to experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow character arcs (for discovery writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let your characters' growth and choices suggest natural conclusion points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to how characters change during drafting; their trajectories often point directly to appropriate endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look for recurring themes (for discovery writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice motifs or ideas that recur in your draft to identify meaningful endings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Themes unearthed during discovery writing can indicate what kind of resolution will best reflect the story's concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take notes on subconscious seeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Record fleeting thoughts about possible endings while drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your subconscious may generate viable ending ideas; keep notes so you can revisit and develop them later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible plotting (for hybrid writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a general idea of your ending but stay open to organic changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid writers benefit from broad plans combined with openness; this lets character discoveries alter planned beats when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone mapping (for hybrid writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify key moments your ending needs to hit without plotting every detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set essential endpoints or emotional beats the ending must achieve, then allow flexibility in how you reach them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-plot balance (for hybrid writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let character decisions influence your planned plot points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure characters' choices meaningfully drive the plot toward the ending rather than merely serving pre-plotted events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular revision (for hybrid writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust your ending plans as your story evolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisit and revise the ending in light of new drafts, making sure it still fits character arcs, themes and plot developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing your ending (checklist + beta readers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate your ending with a checklist and outside feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: 'Does it feel true to your characters? Have you resolved the main conflict? Does it satisfy the story promises you made? Will readers find it emotionally satisfying? Does it reflect your themes? Would a different type of ending work better?' Also solicit beta readers if you’re too close to the manuscript to be objective.
